review.rationale: The supplied Gold is a coherent independent expectation for this planning-only bundle. REQ-001 and AC-001–AC-003 consistently require live, readonly wrapper counts from the existing internal limiter, preservation of Promise/scheduling/clearQueue behavior, and runtime plus compile-time regressions. The complete supplied source supports the exact four-file writable binding: index.js owns the wrapper, index.d.ts is the directly exported maintained declaration, and test.js plus index.test-d.ts own the regressions. package.json establishes xo && ava && tsd as the existing verification entry point without requiring a configuration edit. Stable requirement, acceptance, and task keys agree across the specification and Gold; the specification requires independent verification dependent on implementation and both relationships to cover all required acceptance criteria. The allowed implementer and verifier have appropriate project-scoped active trusted claims, including data.change, domain.state, integration.async, integration.consumer, JavaScript, TypeScript, contract and testing capabilities; the verifier additionally has testing.verification. Pending security.authorization claims are not needed for this change and are not treated as trusted. A separate active project reviewer is configured for the earlier scenario-coverage prerequisite. No material unresolved Decision is supplied for this case, so ready with no blocking reasons is appropriate; no hypothetical input is treated as a human Decision. Gold and preview release fingerprints match, and the supplied provenance explains the distinct manifest/evaluation digest domains and trim-only PRD persistence. Historical operations are explicitly old-version records, not candidates on this bundle, and project reuse preserves rather than copies scoped attestations. The original preparation-status fields do not negate the subsequently supplied frozen release and team evidence. This approval reviews the supplied records only: it does not attest human confirmation, independently recompute Service digests, execute checks, approve task dispatch, or infer candidate performance.
